rationale: The objective is the median over 3 separately profiled runs of the max-rank summed NCCL kernel duration for one accumulated step (step_ms <= 1.05x baseline, i.e. <= 121.95 ms vs original 116.14). Those NCCL kernels are exactly the 13 DDP gradient-bucket SUM allreduces that flow through the two c10d::allreduce_ dispatch sites selected here (group f833b57a373d8262a384 = call d0938de87369efd500322679, 12x 28,351,488 B buckets; group 8525af72c631b94e3dd0 = call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b, 1x 157,541,376 B bucket; full 497,759,232 B fp32 payload per rank, PG 0, stream 17), so this joint pair is the complete editable surface of the metric and shares one dispatch target; replacing only one site would split the reduction path and lose the phase-end marker carried by the large-bucket site. Measured composition of the 38.09 ms baseline on this revision: a transfer floor of ~34.6 ms (current execution_timeline: back-to-back non-waiting bucket kernels 1.93-1.99 ms per 27 MiB and 10.45-10.47 ms for the 150 MiB bucket; collective_calibration at the exact sizes gives 1.995 ms and 10.6 ms medians, i.e. ~14.2-14.9 GB/s logical on both LL and SIMPLE) plus ~2-7 ms of cross-rank arrival skew paid as in-kernel spin-wait (current execution_timeline clock-aligned evidence: rank 1 submitted the first allreduce 6213 us after rank 0's first kernel start, so rank 0's first kernel ran 8114 us ~= 6213 + 1929; per-run waiter-vs-non-waiter rank sums in the original baseline diagnostics are 42.69/35.92, 38.09/34.70, 38.40/35.21). Rejected with measured cause: (1) protocol forcing - the previous joint candidate (trial-3ca928eb87) forced NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE on a dedicated group and every kernel remained ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_f32_RING_LL (grid 2x544, stream 21), and calibration shows SIMPLE would gain nothing anyway (transport-bound SHM/PCIe pair: peer_access 0 in both directions, no NVLink); (2) second-process-group substitution per call - the same failed trial proved per-call host cost is toxic: bucket submission pacing went 2.6 ms -> 5.5 ms, early-rank per-bucket kernels 1.9 -> 5.8 ms (nsys previous-after), step_ms 116 -> 229 (limit 121.95) and the objective 38.09 -> 56.33 with rank asymmetry, while correctness stayed bitwise-exact (max_abs_error 0.0, coverage 12+1) - so the boundary itself is proven safe, the implementation approach was the failure; (3) coalescing the 13 buckets into one collective - saves at most ~1-2 ms of per-op overhead but forfeits the measured ~10.9-11.1 ms comm/compute overlap by delaying comm past the backward tail, risking the step_ms constraint, and per-bucket Work return semantics make deferral unsafe; (4) reduced-precision reduction - violates grad_atol 1e-6 / rtol 1e-4 fidelity scope. The one remaining actionable, evidence-backed component of the metric is the arrival-skew wait: keep every collective identical (same group, same SUM, same tensors, bitwise-unchanged outputs, real parent Work returned) and additionally align the ranks before the first bucket of each reduction phase with a non-NCCL CPU rendezvous (dist.barrier on the gloo group already held in adapter state as state['control'], created in prepare and already used by before_run outside timing), so the early rank's wait is spent in a host barrier that launches no NCCL kernel instead of inside a counted NCCL kernel. No new process group, no per-call host work on the 12 non-first calls (the proven failure mode), no setup inside timing (the gloo group already exists; the state machine is symmetric and deterministic on both ranks because the observed 12x28,351,488 B + 1x157,541,376 B sequence is identical per rank).
hypothesis: Replacing both c10d::allreduce_ sites with parent-exact per-call passthrough (identical SUM allreduce on the caller's own process group, real (Tensor[], Work) returned, bitwise-identical gradients so the atol=0/rtol=0 replica check and serial-reference checks are unaffected) plus one gloo barrier on state['control'] executed only at the first bucket of each reduction phase (detected symmetrically: the first 28,351,488 B call of an invocation, i.e. the first call ever or the first small-bucket call after the 157,541,376 B call, with an idle-gap guard for robustness) will move the cross-rank arrival skew out of NCCL kernel durations: the first bucket's kernel should drop from the observed 8.1 ms (profiled; clean waiter deltas 2.9-6.8 ms per run) toward the ~1.99 ms transfer time, and the max-rank median objective should fall from 38.09 ms toward ~35.5-36.5 ms (~2-2.6 ms, ~6%), bounded below by the ~34.6 ms transfer floor. Step_ms should be neutral to slightly better: the early rank waits in the host barrier instead of inside its kernel and its communication train then ends earlier, the late rank adds only ~0.1-0.5 ms barrier latency, and the max-rank wall that defines step_ms is set by the late rank; the 5.8 ms constraint headroom is not consumed. Explicit unknowns, treated as hypotheses to test: (a) the clean-run skew distribution is only sampled n=3 (waiter deltas 2.9/3.2/6.8 ms; if clean skew is near the low end the benefit shrinks toward run-to-run noise); (b) gloo barrier exit jitter may leave 0.1-0.5 ms residual wait inside the first kernel, and the residual per-bucket submit skew (~0.6 ms/bucket under profiler hooks, ~0.1 ms clean) remains unaddressed; (c) blocking the reducer/autograd thread until the peer arrives must not stall the early rank's own backward pipeline more than the in-kernel wait it replaces - profiled evidence suggests the early rank's comm train shortens by more than the added block, but this is unverified without hooks; (d) phase-start detection must hold across warmup, repeats, continuous_steps=2 and the 3 profiled diagnostic runs, including the unobserved first-iteration DDP bucket layout before rebuild (discovery only observed the stable 12+1 steady state) - a misdetection adds one spurious ~0.3 ms barrier, not a deadlock, because detection is deterministic and symmetric on both ranks; (e) any accidental per-call Python overhead on the 12 non-first calls would reproduce the previous trial's serialization failure and must be kept off that path. If the measured skew turns out to be inherently small in clean runs, the floor-bound metric leaves this boundary with no further evidence-supported lever, and the result should be reported as such rather than escalating to riskier transport changes that the failed trial already falsified.
